title: Two papers disagree on the finding. (No hand-audit recorded for this pair)
explanation: Claim A identifies a non-linear, U-shaped association where moderate use correlates with the lowest anxiety, directly conflicting with Claim B's finding of a linear association between social media use and anxiety.
a_text: Two large cohort studies observed a non-linear, U-shaped relationship where moderate social media use was associated with lower anxiety symptoms than persistently low or high use.
b_text: Social media use has a very small linear association with anxiety outcomes in young people (pooled r = 0.093, 95% CI [0.059, 0.126]).
